pedal: Boss PH-3 Phase Shifter — Res, above all in Rise and Fall (mono)
comment: Why: with Res up, NAM-X's Rise and Fall are far from the pedal (a blind test, 2026-11-11: the pedal's peaks 16-25 dB over a baseline 8 dB under the dry, the model's about 13 over a baseline near it), and Res was never measured in those modes. Takes are grouped by knob setting: within a group only the Mode switch moves, so every mode sees exactly the same Rate, Depth and Res, and the 8 Stage take of a group says what loop gain that Res position really gave (in-between angles needn't be exact). The mode order runs forward in one group and backward in the next, so the switch never jumps back. Signals: nine quiet sines together (each tone's level on the output is the filter at its frequency at every moment; in Rise and Fall the pattern slides past each tone, which draws its whole shape); a sweep where the phaser stands still (Rate 7:00); the funk excerpt in one validation group. Part A: the Res ladder at seven positions, finer in the upper half where the model is worst, every mode, then the loudest setting again 12 dB up. Part D: the sweep stopped, Res at three positions (a still picture of the resonance; whether Rise stops at all is itself a question). Parts B and C: Depth at 12:00 and fully down. Part E: a fast Rate. Part V: two settings of the user's choice, in no fit. Clock positions: 7:00 = fully counter-clockwise, 5:00 = fully clockwise. The Mode switch's order on the pedal is 4, 8, 10, 12 Stage, Fall, Rise, Step: the groups follow it.
